summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with fever, chills, nausea, and worsening abdominal pain, two days after discharge from a prior admission for chronic pancreatitis complicated by Klebsiella bacteremia. She presented with a swollen, erythematous left arm and was found to have clinical signs of cellulitis and possible bacteremia, though blood cultures remained negative. She was treated with IV vancomycin and ceftriaxone. A new PICC line was placed in the right arm for antibiotic administration. Imaging showed persistent thrombosis in the left axillary and brachial veins with recanalization of the subclavian vein. She was kept NPO initially for pancreatitis management, then advanced to oral intake as symptoms improved. Warfarin was restarted with enoxaparin bridging due to concerns about absorption during flares. Reiki therapy helped manage anxiety. She improved clinically, became afebrile, and was discharged home on a six-day course of IV antibiotics via OPAT, warfarin, and her baseline medications.
problems: Other septicemia due to gram-negative organisms
